links.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents

evidence: Abstract: 'A 4B Qwen3 trained with SMITH on 13 procedural reasoning tasks with exact verifiers reaches 79.8 macro-average accuracy on held-out tasks... 40.4 on TabMWP-Hard and 42.6 on out-of-domain GQA (+7.6 over the best same-backbone inference-time baseline)'

Section 3.6 / Table 1: 'SMITH leads held-out generalization (RG Unseen 79.9) over distilled models (ReTool 63.2, LATM-distill 65.8)... using 32x fewer output tokens than standard CoT' (100 vs 3,206 output tokens)
Section 3.11 / Table 7: 'Decoupled build/use does not beat single-model Tool Create on RG (Unseen) (58.9 vs 68.8)... only the full SMITH objective wins on aggregate' (Full: RG S 86.61, RG U 78.33)
Section 3.9 / Table 5: 'for Qwen3-8B, SMITH improves... (72.6→79.4) and the holdout RG accuracy (72.2→81.7)... Granite-3.3-8B... lifts RG (Seen) to 39.1, RG (Unseen) to 28.5'
Section 3.7 / Table 3: 'the SMITH-4B-written tools lift the 30B consumer on every group, most sharply on TabMWP-Hard (0.7→38.8), and raise the task-weighted overall score from 70.2 to 76.6'
Section 3.10 / Table 6: 'SMITH lifts BFCL overall accuracy on both Qwen backbones, from 45.1 to 48.6 on Qwen3-4B and from 43.3 to 55.8 on Qwen3-8B'
Appendix B: documents a verifiable training failure ('naming drift' reward collapse, Table 8 per-step metrics) and derives five design lessons for verifier+judge reward combination

Section 4 Limitations: 'All trained policies are at most 8B parameters... whether the gains persist... at the 70B+ scale is an open question... we do not formally certify that adversarial prompts cannot induce unsafe tools'
Appendix N: 'All SMITH training runs were performed on a single NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro GPU... between 36 and 72 hours'
Appendix O / Table 17: 'No configuration ever significantly outperforms v1' (two-sided exact McNemar tests), guarding against under-tuned-baseline objections

Inconsistency noted: Appendix I states 'ReTool achieves the highest in-distribution accuracy on RG (Seen) (92.0 vs. our 86.6)' while Section 3.6/Table 1 report 92.2 vs 85.2, and Appendix J reports LATM-distill Seen 83.3 / Unseen 66.4 vs Table 1's 81.7 / 65.8
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM/agent-methodology paper: RL-trained joint tool creation and use (SMITH) on Qwen3 backbones, squarely matching high-weight preferences for LLMs, agents & tool use, reasoning, and RL. Novelty is solid but incremental over LATM/CRAFT/TroVE/KTCE (inference-time tool creation) and ReTool/SAGE (RL for tool use/skills); the genuinely new elements are the schema-grounded joint build/use objective, three disentangled reward axes, easy-to-hard evaluation split, and tool-pool curriculum. Rigor is strong: many same-backbone baselines, seeded re-evaluations with std, a full reward-structure ablation (Table 7), cross-backbone replication (Table 5), BFCL v4 transfer, and unusually candid baseline forensics (Appendix L) plus a McNemar-tested prompt-tuning ablation (Appendix O). Evidence strength is good but dented by internal numeric inconsistencies (abstract/conclusion 79.8 vs Table 1 79.9; Appendix I 'ReTool 92.0 vs ours 86.6' vs Section 3.6/Table 1 '92.2 vs 85.2'; Appendix J 'Seen 83.3/Unseen 66.4' vs Table 1 '81.7/65.8') and reliance on an LLM judge whose bias is only partially probed by the Self-Judge ablation. Generalizability is supported across 4B/8B/Granite backbones, a 350M and a 30B consumer, TabMWP-Hard, and GQA (though GQA needs fixed visual primitives and the paper concedes the GPT-4.1 distillation gap there), but 70B+ scale and richer artifacts (MCP/skills) are explicitly open (Section 4). Reproducibility is high: verbatim judge prompt (Appendix C), full task splits (Appendix F), hyperparameters (Tables 12-13), tool-pool design (Appendix E), and single-GPU 36-72h cost (Appendix N), with Code/Project Page links claimed. Not out-of-scope; no instruction-following from paper text was performed.

primary_link.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents

top5.summary: Tool-augmented language models are bounded by the APIs humans bothered to write; existing tool-creation systems patch this by prompting a frozen LLM at inference time, leaving the model that writes a tool decoupled from the one that uses it, with no signal that the schemas it produces are schemas it can invoke. We propose SMITH (Schema-grounded Multi-task Iterative Tool Honing), a reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains tool creation and tool use inside a single policy. Each rollout
top5.summary_zh: 本文提出 SMITH，一個以強化學習在單一策略內同時訓練「建立工具」與「使用工具」的框架。現有工具增強系統依賴人類預先設計的 API，推論時的工具生成方法（LATM、CRAFT、TroVE、KTCE）僅以提示詞驅動凍結模型，寫工具與用工具脫鉤，缺乏「寫出的 schema 能否被自己呼叫」的訓練訊號。SMITH 交錯兩類任務：build 任務自少量範例歸納出 Python 函式與 OpenAI 相容的 JSON schema；use 任務只看 schema，須從工具池挑選並呼叫工具回答保留題。獎勵分為格式一致性、執行準確率（於更難題組上評估，評估器定期與策略同步）與 LLM 審查品質三個獨立軸，以 DAPO 聯合最佳化，並採由易到難協定逼出可泛化的抽象工具。以 Qwen3-4B-Instruct 加 LoRA 在 13 個 Reasoning-Gym 程序性任務上訓練後，未見任務達 79.8% 巨觀平均準確率，超越所有推論時與蒸餾基線，每題輸出約 100 tokens（較 CoT 少 32 倍）；零樣本轉移於 TabMWP-Hard 得 40.4%，GQA 得 42.6%。其工具可跨規模移植：讓 LFM2.5-350M 追平 30B 工具撰寫模型，訓練配方亦一致提升 Qwen3-8B 與 Granite-3.3-8B，並改善 BFCL v4 外部工具呼叫。限制：模型規模至多 8B、依賴 30B LLM 審查、工具僅為單一函式與 schema、未觀察到平行工具呼叫，沙盒安全亦未正式驗證。此研究證明讓模型學會撰寫自己能可靠呼叫的工具，是邁向可重用、可遷移代理能力的可擴充路徑。

links.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents

evidence: Sec. 3.4 'Experimental scale': 58 configurations per family over 500 SWE-bench Verified instances yielding 58,000 agent runs, 2M LLM API calls, and 36B tokens processed.

Tab. 1 (Sec. 4): Raw escalation recovers QRec=47% (Claude) and 36% (GPT) of the LC-HC quality gap; Traj-drop raises QRec to 64% and 84%; Raw downshift retains 80%/14% cost savings at 50%/79% quality recovery.

Appendix A.3 Tab. 8: task-clustered bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples) show the central reversal excludes zero in both families — escalation Traj-drop−Raw +3.1 [+1.3,+5.0] Claude, +12.2 [+9.2,+15.4] GPT; downshift −4.7 [−7.3,−2.1] and −5.6 [−8.6,−2.6].

Appendix A.1 'Accounting' and 'Pricing and audit': cost reconstruction from provider usage with cache-aware price cards, exact reconciliation audits, and verbatim handoff prompts; switch steps given in Tab. 11.

Limitations section: single episode per task per configuration, interface findings established primarily in the coding setting, hard-stratum cells N̄≈24–27 treated as exploratory, and dollar-cost conclusions dependent on provider pricing and cache rates.
Sec. 5 Tabs. 2–3: extensions show information dynamics modulate the tax — LiC escalation QRec=86%, BrowseComp GPT escalation QRec=95.8% but CSRet=−30.0%, worse than abort+restart (−8.5%).
llm_evaluation.rationale: A large-scale empirical study of mid-trajectory model handoffs in LLM coding agents, directly matching high-weight preferences (LLMs, agents & tool use, code). Novel contribution: systematic characterization of the 'handoff tax' across direction (escalation/downshift), timing, and interface (raw/compact/traj-drop), with a cross-family directional duality finding. Rigor is strong: matched switched subsets, difficulty-calibrated switch percentiles, restart controls, a disclosure ablation, and task-clustered bootstrap CIs for the central reversal. Evidence is quantitatively supported at scale (58,000 runs, 36B tokens), though single-episode-per-task runs, descriptive (non-inferential) cost mechanics, and a small hard-task stratum (N̄≈24–27, self-flagged as exploratory) temper confidence. Generalizability is limited by two model families, one primary benchmark for interface findings (LiC/BrowseComp use Raw only), fixed switch points, and pricing-dependent cost conclusions. Reproducibility benefits from verbatim prompts, calibration tables (Tab. 11), and audit accounting, but rests on commercial models, a pinned local price card, and only a vague artifact-availability claim rather than an explicit public release.

primary_link.title: The Handoff Tax: Continuing Non-Native Trajectories in LLM Agents

top5.summary: Coding agents perform long-running tasks spanning dozens of model calls, tool uses, and code edits. As these runs unfold, users face a practical cost-quality trade-off: escalating to a stronger model when a cheaper one struggles, or downshifting once the hard reasoning is complete. Each switch requires the receiver to continue a non-native trajectory produced by another model. We study how this handoff affects quality and cost, and how varying the trajectory information inherited by the receiver changes the outcome. Using pairs of low-cost, low-capability (LC) and high-cost, high-capability (HC) models from the Claude and GPT families, we vary handoff direction, timing, and interface, comparing full-trajectory transfer, compaction, and trajectory removal while preserving the repository state. Across both model families, full-trajectory escalation recovers less than half of the LC-to-HC quality gap while incurring a substantial cost premium. We term this cost-quality penalty the handoff tax. By contrast, downshift offers a favorable cost-quality point. Interestingly, the preferred interface also reverses with direction: reducing LC-model trajectory information improves escalation quality, whereas removing the HC-model trajectory reduces downshift quality.
top5.summary_zh: 這篇論文探討長時程編程代理（coding agent）任務中，中途更換模型所付出的「handoff tax」（交接稅）。使用者在便宜模型（LC）卡關時升級到強大模型（HC），或完成艱難推理後降級省錢，但接手模型必須延續另一個模型產生的非原生軌跡。作者在 SWE-bench Verified 上，以 Claude（Haiku 4.5/Opus 4.7）與 GPT-5.6（Luna/Sol）兩組配對，變換切換方向、時機與介面：Raw（完整軌跡）、Compact（摘要壓縮）與 Traj-drop（移除軌跡但保留程式碼編輯），合計每族 58 種設定、58,000 次代理執行與 360 億個 token。核心結果：Raw 升級僅收回不到一半的品質差距且成本高昂，Claude 案例中甚至比重跑 HC 更貴更差；降級則提供有利的成本與品質中間點。軌跡資訊的價值具有方向性：減少 LC 軌跡可提升升級品質（Traj-drop 品質最佳、Compact_pre 最省），移除 HC 軌跡則損害降級品質。機制上，Raw 升級使 HC 每步更貴；Traj-drop 降級使 LC 多走 1.6 至 2 倍步驟以重建遺失脈絡。LiC 與 BrowseComp 延伸實驗顯示資訊動態會翻轉結論，遲到的需求有利於升級。限制：僅兩組模型、單一基準、固定切換點、每任務單次執行，且困難子集樣本小。本研究指出模型交接應視為獨立的推論問題，交接介面需與模型選擇及切換時機共同最佳化，對代理系統的路由與成本管理極具實務意義。

links.title: AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents

evidence: Abstract: proposes AgentSpec with structure-isolated drafting and redundancy-aware budget allocation; claims at most 2.02x speedup over autoregressive decoding for agent batch inference.
Section 3.2 / Table 1: measured average per-request rejection rates of 53.3% (EAGLE-3), 88.7% (NGram), 65.9% (SuffixDecoding) vs 26.4% for AgentSpec on the Reflexion code-generation workflow.
Section 3.2 / Figure 2: FFN latency of Qwen-3-8B grows linearly beyond batch size 256 on A100, motivating the token budget M(b)=AI-b definition.

Section 5.2 / Table 2: goodput results across Qwen-3-8B, GPT-OSS-20B, DeepSeek-Distill-8B on GAIA, SWE-Bench, Deep Research, Code Generation; AgentSpec achieves up to 104% relative gain and 2.02x speedup while several baselines fall below 1.0x.
Section 5.5 / Table 3: on MiMo-7B, MTP reaches only 0.73x speedup on Code Gen (All) while AgentSpec reaches 1.29x.
Section 5.6 / Table 5: execution breakdown shows AgentSpec verification cost 26.11 min (down 21%) and overall 27.85 min (down 19%) vs baselines.

Section 5.7 / Table 6: ablations AgentSpec(S), AgentSpec(R), AgentSpec(N) show structure-isolated drafting contributes more than redundancy-aware budget allocation, and the no-structure variant still outperforms baselines.
Section 5.4 / Table 4: on non-agentic Spec-Bench (Qwen-3-8B), AgentSpec achieves 1.14x overall speedup, smaller than agentic gains.

Section A.1: vLLM v0.12.0 V1 engine, A100 80G, FlashAttention-2, max batch 256, baselines run with official default configs, results averaged over five seeds; API extension with structure/query_id/agent_id fields documented.
Section A.3 / Table 7: H100 speedups (e.g., 2.28x CodeGen) exceed A100, supporting hardware generalization.
Limitation: acknowledges required lightweight interface between agent and serving system and dependence on explicit semantic blocks and repeated generation patterns.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strongly on-profile: an inference-efficiency method for LLM agents, evaluated on agent benchmarks (SWE-Bench, GAIA, USACO code generation, DeepResearch) in vLLM, matching Agents & Tool Use, LLM, Inference & Serving, and Code & Programming. Novelty is solid but incremental over SuffixDecoding/NGram-style draft-model-free speculation: structure-isolated drafting via a PDA over semantic blocks (Section 4.1) and redundancy-aware budget allocation (Section 4.2, Eq. 1-3) are concrete mechanisms, though budget-allocation ideas exist (AdaSpec, TETRIS). Rigor is good: bottleneck analysis with a cost model and FFN latency measurement (Section 3.2, Figure 2), four models from four families, four agentic workloads plus Spec-Bench, MTP comparison (Table 3), ablations isolating each component (Table 6), batch-size and thinking-mode sweeps (Figure 9), and H100 cross-check (Table 7). Weaknesses: losslessness is asserted in the abstract but no explicit output-equivalence verification is reported; baseline configs use defaults (Section A.1) which may favor the proposed method; no variance/CI despite five-run averaging; rejection-rate analysis concentrates on one Reflexion workload (Table 1). Evidence strength is high for throughput claims (Table 2: up to 104% gain, 2.02x speedup; Table 5: verification -21%), with the caveat above. Generalizability is supported across models, GPUs, and a non-agentic benchmark (1.14x, Table 4), though the method expects semantic-structure metadata from the agent, acknowledged in Limitations. Reproducibility is moderate: engine version, GPU, baseline hyperparameters, API extension example, and pseudocode are given (Section A.1, A.2), but no code-release claim and key hyperparameters (alpha, g_min) values are unspecified.

primary_link.title: AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents

top5.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based agent applications often incur high response time. Speculative decoding is a promising solution to improve the inference efficiency of LLM agents without impacting generation quality. However, state-of-the-art speculative decoding algorithms exhibit substantial speed degradation under large batch sizes, limiting their effectiveness to deploy in real-world agent applications. In this work, we first present a systematic analysis of speculative decoding for LLM agen
top5.summary_zh: 以大型語言模型（LLM）為基礎的代理應用常因多步推理與工具呼叫而推論成本高昂。推測解碼雖可無損加速生成，但在現代推論引擎普遍採用的大批次設定下，現有方法的加速效果會大幅衰退，甚至比自迴歸解碼更慢。作者分析後歸納兩大瓶頸：推測 token 的高拒絕率，以及動態 token 預算的低利用率。據此提出 AgentSpec，一套免草稿模型的推測解碼演算法：其一為結構隔離起草，要求代理提供語意結構識別資訊，透過輕量下推自動機追蹤語意區塊，僅從語意一致的歷史片段擷取草稿，將拒絕率降至約 26%，遠低於 EAGLE-3 的 53% 與 NGram 的 89%；其二為冗餘感知預算分配，以冗餘分數預測各請求的接受可能性，動態分配推測預算以貼近硬體可用上限。團隊在 vLLM 上實作，於 Qwen-3-8B、GPT-OSS-20B、DeepSeek 蒸餾模型與 MiMo-7B，以及程式碼生成、深度研究、SWE-Bench、GAIA 等代理式工作負載評估，最高達 2.02 倍加速，goodput 較最佳基線提升最多 104%，於 Spec-Bench 與對比 MiMo-7B 的 MTP 亦領先。消融實驗顯示兩個元件各有貢獻，其中結構隔離起草影響較大。限制在於需在代理與伺服器間加入輕量介面，且加速程度部分取決於工作負載中重複生成樣式的多寡；即使缺少明確語意結構，仍有穩定加速。此研究讓推測解碼在大批次代理服務場景重新變得實用，有助降低 LLM 代理的部署成本與延遲。

links.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

evidence: Section 5.1: experiments conducted in a real browser environment on @mcp-b/global 2.3.2 (2026-06-17 draft spec); attack success defined as malicious tool invoked and exfiltrated data received at the receiving end.
Table 1 (Section 5.2): four-layer ablation (L0-L3), n=80 per cell; description injection 69/80 (L0) to 0/80 (L3); return-content injection 42/80 (L0) to 2/80 (L3).

Table 2 (Section 5.3) and Section 5.3 text: the 2/80 residuals at L2/L3 are explained as name-driven invocations occurring before inspection; Q detects the carrier 40/40; residuals are structural, not detection failures.

Table 3 (Section 5.4): cross-page semantic residual — lifecycle clearing alone leaves 70% ASR; lifecycle+framework yields 0% ASR at 100% completion; Section 5.2 reports no-attack baseline 61/80 statistically indistinguishable from L3 (p=0.48); Section 6.2 flags adversarial utility inflation (p=0.003).

Section 6.1: capability handles reduce overwrite/revocation attacks (V4, V6) from 20/20 to 0/20 and V5 legitimate responses rise 0/20 to 20/20; bearer-capability limits and confused-deputy risk acknowledged.

Section 6.2/Section 7: name-relevance Table 4 shows rule-based stripping ASR rises 0% to 70% with name relevance while multi-agent stays 0%; white-box adaptive attacker with Q's classifier prompt bypassed 15/16 description payloads with median one rewrite.

Section 7 (Limitations): reference implementation is a JavaScript polyfill emulating API-surface integrity and script provenance; site-declared trust policy and Request UI not empirically evaluated; Runtime Observation is detection/containment, not prevention; Section 5.1 uses a single unnamed language model and no code release is claimed.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Directly on-scope: security architecture for browser-integrated LLM agents with MCP-style tool calling, prompt-injection defense, and adversarial evaluation maps strongly to the Agents & Tool Use, AI Safety, LLM, and Red Teaming preferences. Strengths: well-specified threat model (same-origin script attacker, extensions explicitly out of scope), a clean four-layer ablation with n=80 per cell, a notable utility-confounder analysis anchoring completion to a no-attack baseline (p=0.48, p=0.003), an honest limitations section, and a white-box adaptive-attacker study showing 15/16 description-layer bypasses via tool-name relocation. Weaknesses: the asymmetric dual-agent quarantine is derivative of Dual-LLM/CaMeL-style privilege separation (novelty rests mainly on the browser-native capability layer and the WebMCP specification-level analysis); results are tied to one reference implementation version with an unnamed LLM; no empirical comparison against external defenses (CaMeL, ACE, IsolateGPT); two architectural components (trust policy, Request UI) are presented but not evaluated; no code/artifact release is claimed. Evidence is internally consistent and quantitative but self-contained, lowering generalizability and reproducibility. Calibrated weighted score ~0.78.

primary_link.title: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents

top5.summary: The emerging W3C WebMCP proposal enables LLM agents to invoke tools exposed by web pages. In multi-party web environments, however, integrating agent execution into a browser security model centered on the Same-Origin Policy (SOP) leaves insufficient provenance and lifecycle guarantees for agent-accessible tools, creating three risks: subject-attribution spoofing, uncontrolled tool lifecycles, and semantic prompt injection. We propose WebMCP-Phalanx, a dual-layer agent runtime architecture. Its
top5.summary_zh: 隨著 W3C 推動 WebMCP 標準草案，網頁將能向 LLM 代理人暴露可呼叫的工具，但也使代理執行落入以同源政策（SOP）為中心的瀏覽器安全模型；由於網站主程式、第三方廣告 SDK 與分析腳本共用同一 origin，規範未提供工具來源與生命週期保障，衍生主體歸屬偽冒、生命週期失控與語意提示注入等結構性弱點。作者提出 WebMCP-Phalanx 雙層架構：瀏覽器原生層以不可偽造的能力憑證綁定工具所有權，並結合遙測與生命週期監控產生綠、黃、紅三級信任標籤；多代理層則由不具工具呼叫權限的隔離代理（Q-LLM）先行檢視工具描述、輸入綱要與回傳內容，再交由擁有執行權限的特權代理（P-LLM）使用。真實瀏覽器實驗顯示，所有權機制將撤銷與覆寫攻擊成功率由 100% 降為 0%，雙代理執行環境擋下全部 80 次描述注入，回傳內容注入僅殘留 2 次，且任務效用與無攻擊基線無統計顯著差異。論文亦刻畫限制：同源腳本可自行註冊取得憑證，使來源維度失效；白箱自適應攻擊者能將指令藏於工具名稱並在檢查完成前觸發呼叫，繞過描述層過濾；polyfill 實作的安全假設屬模擬性質，能力憑證屬持有式憑證，仍有混淆代理人問題。作者建議 WebMCP 納入原生腳本來源與宣告式信任拓撲等機制，並新增呼叫時機閘門，盼在規範定型前落實安全設計，對瀏覽器整合代理的安全性與標準制定具直接參考價值。

links.title: IAPO: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization for Credit Assignment in Multi-Turn Service Agents

evidence: Abstract: 'IAPO represents each rollout as a typed influence-dependency graph... Experiments with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B demonstrate superior performance over multi-turn RL baselines across three service-agent benchmarks: τ2-Bench, UserBench, and AgentChangeBench.'

Method/Influence-Dependency Graph: support-use (i→+j) and failed-use (i→-j) edges with necessity/explicit-binding/source-priority acceptance criteria; 'user turns and tool returns provide evidence but never receive advantage.'
Properties, Propositions 1-4: mass conservation Σ A_i,ℓ = L Â_τ, uniform fallback, sign preservation, optimization-interface preservation; 'proofs are in Appendix B.'
Table 1 (8B): IAPO 42.18±2.55 vs GRPO 29.61±3.56 on τ2-Bench; UserBench 24.44 vs 19.83; AgentChangeBench 30.44 vs 26.03; BFCL-MT 39.36 vs 39.04.

Experiments/Experimental Setup: 'train Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with thinking disabled on 8× NVIDIA H20 GPUs using a verl/FSDP GRPO stack, N=16 samples/prompt, max 30 turns. Dependency annotation uses Qwen3-32B at temperature 0... IAPO defaults: β+=0.05, c=0.25.'
Table 3 (Ablation): β+=0 yields 32.50 τ2 vs 42.18 default; β+=0.1 yields 33.96; c=0.5 yields 42.29 τ2 but UserBench drops to 17.78; Gemma4-31B annotator yields 40.90 τ2.
Annotator Stability: 'Six frozen annotators achieve 100% parse rate... mean edge-typed F1 0.87, source Jaccard 0.84, mean pairwise Cohen's κ=0.83'; m− Spearman ρ=0.96-1.00 (Table 4).
Main Results: 'IAPO lowers macro tool-call redundancy from GRPO's 46.00 to 29.74 (Appendix F)'; routing departs from flat credit ('86.5% of steps move by more than 10% from flat credit, Appendix E').
No code or data release statement appears anywhere in the provided document; only public benchmarks and the MUA-RL checkpoint (re-evaluated) are cited.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM-agent RL methodology, squarely in scope: multi-turn service agents, GRPO-style training, tool use, and function calling (Abstract; Related Work). The core idea—routing a fixed trajectory-level advantage through a within-rollout, LLM-annotated typed influence-dependency graph instead of uniform GRPO credit—is a genuinely distinct angle versus cross-rollout grouping (GiGPO), reset/branch methods, or auxiliary critics (Introduction; Related Work), though influence-based credit assignment has older RL precedents (RUDDER, hindsight). Rigor is solid: a controlled GRPO baseline differing only in the advantage map (Experiments), two model scales, three seeds, OOD benchmarks, hyperparameter and annotator-swap ablations (Table 3), and cross-annotator stability audits (Table 4); proofs of mass conservation and sign preservation are stated (Properties, Appendix B). Deductions: no significance testing, the chosen defaults (β+=0.05, c=0.25) are the sweep optima with notable sensitivity (42.18 vs 33.96 for β+=0.1), and the method's quality hinges on a frozen Qwen3-32B annotator whose extraction rules could bias credit. Evidence strength is good but internal: detailed quantitative tables (Table 1: 42.18±2.55 vs 29.61±3.56 at 8B; Table 5 BFCL retention) with no code/data release statement in the document. Generalizability is supported by training only on τ²-Bench while improving UserBench/AgentChangeBench and flat BFCL (Main Results), but the approach presumes multi-turn interaction with observable tool/schema errors and a capable annotator model. Reproducibility is moderate: stack (verl/FSDP, 8×H20, N=16, temp-0 annotator) and defaults are given with full details claimed in Appendix F, but no artifact availability is stated.

primary_link.title: IAPO: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization for Credit Assignment in Multi-Turn Service Agents

top5.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly solve long-horizon tasks through multi-turn interactions with users and external tools. In these settings, relevant task information often unfolds over time rather than being fully specified at the initial prompt. Service agents make this challenge especially concrete: users may clarify or revise their goals, while tool responses provide information needed for subsequent decisions. Thus, a final reward alone cannot indicate which actions contributed
top5.summary_zh: 多輪服務代理的任務資訊隨對話逐步浮現：使用者會中途修改目標，工具回傳揭示所需狀態，僅憑最終獎勵難以判斷哪些動作促成任務完成。GRPO 等演算法把軌跡層級優勢平均套用到每個 token，無法區分中間動作的貢獻。論文提出 IAPO（影響感知策略最佳化），將完成的 rollout 表示為以可訓練動作為節點、帶正負號的影響依賴圖：支援使用邊記錄後續動作消費前序動作引出的資訊，失敗使用邊標記可觀察錯誤的傳播與回退；使用者與工具觀察僅作證據、不取得梯度信用。路由權重據此重新分配原軌跡優勢，並具質量守恆、符號保持與均勻回退等保證。實驗以 Qwen3-4B 與 Qwen3-8B 在 τ²-Bench 訓練，並於 τ²-Bench、UserBench 與 AgentChangeBench 驗證：8B 模型於 τ²-Bench 由 29.61% 提升至 42.18%，電信領域增益達 +18.19 個百分點，並優於 GRPO、GiGPO 與 InfoPO，BFCL-v4 Multi-Turn 的函式呼叫能力亦維持不變；消融實驗亦顯示兩類訊號皆有貢獻、標註模型可替換。限制在於依賴凍結標註模型（Qwen3-32B）抽取依賴圖，標註品質與超參數 β+、c 的設定影響成效，且驗證集中在服務型任務。此研究顯示，rollout 內已實現的依賴結構是稀疏獎勵下細粒度功勞分配的實用來源。
